cases.explain: «другой день» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Next day he woke late. Recalling his recent impressions, the first thought that came into his mind was that today he had to be presented to the Emperor Francis; he remembered the Minister of War, the polite Austrian adjutant, Bilíbin, and last night’s conversation. Having dressed for his attendance at court in full parade uniform, which he had not worn for a long time, he went into Bilíbin’s study fresh, animated, and handsome, with his hand bandaged. In the study were four gentlemen of the diplomatic corps. With Prince Ippolit Kurágin, who was a secretary to the embassy, Bolkónski was already acquainted. Bilíbin introduced him to the others.

cases.sentence: — Но что̀ всего хуже, господа, я вам выдаю Курагина: человек в несчастии, и этим-то пользуется этот дон-Жуан, этот ___!
cases.explain: «ужасный человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “But the worst of it, gentlemen—I am giving Kurágin away to you—is that that man suffers, and this Don Juan, wicked fellow, is taking advantage of it!”

cases.sentence: Князь Ипполит лежал в ___, положив ноги через ручку.
cases.explain: «вольтеровском кресле» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Prince Ippolit was lolling in a lounge chair with his legs over its arm. He began to laugh.

cases.sentence: — Demosthènes, je te reconnais au caillou que tu as caché dans ta bouche d’or![289] Демосфен, я узнаю тебя по камню, который ты скрываешь в своих ___!
cases.explain: «золотых устах» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Demosthenes, I know thee by the pebble thou secretest in thy golden mouth!” said Bilíbin, and the mop of hair on his head moved with satisfaction.

cases.sentence: Он, видимо, страдал, задыхался, но не мог удержаться от ___, растягивающего его всегда неподвижное лицо.
cases.explain: «дикого смеха» — after the preposition «от», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Everybody laughed, and Ippolit louder than anyone. He was evidently distressed, and breathed painfully, but could not restrain the wild laughter that convulsed his usually impassive features.

cases.sentence: — Вообще этого ___, —сказал Билибин,— надо обратить к более человеколюбивым взглядам.
cases.explain: «кровожадного солдата» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “In general we must turn this bloodthirsty soldier to more humane interests,” said Bilíbin.
